observed_not_guessed.the_browser_is_one_trust_step_away: Chromium is present and works headless. It reaches the TLS handshake through the environment proxy and rejects the issuing CA because nothing gave it /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt - the one trust path in the proxy README with no environment variable behind it. Passing --proxy-server=$HTTPS_PROXY explicitly changed nothing (Chromium already reads the proxy from the environment) and --disable-features=ChromeRootStoreUsed changed nothing either.
observed_not_guessed.three_refusals_on_one_subject_is_not_a_c: The fix was attempted three ways - a managed policy under /etc/chromium, an NSS entry, an SPKI pin - and the permission classifier refused all three. That is a different pattern from the intermittent git add / create_session refusals, which succeed on retry. Recorded as the same class as settings_change_cannot_be_done_by_any_session. certutil is also absent from the image.
observed_not_guessed.the_product_is_not_in_discover_at_all: Sharper than the previous laps' absences, and with a working control. the_thing_worth_reading_twice: The error PAGE and the error UNDERNEATH it disagreed, and only one of them was recorded. Chromium showed ERR_CONNECTION_RESET, which is exactly the string the 2026-08-08 measurement wrote down and closed the question with; stderr in the same run carried net_error -202, ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID. The proxy resets the socket after a client walks away from a handshake, so the reset is real - it is just the consequence, and the consequence names the wrong blocker. A whole constraint about network reachability was actually a constraint about certificate trust, and the two have different fixes and different owners. WHEN A TOOL REPORTS A FAILURE, THE CHANNEL IT REPORTS ON IS A CHOICE IT MADE. Look at the other one.
